title: A Stage-Wise Explainable Pipeline for Arteriolar-to-Venular Ratio Estimation and Retinopathy Screening
abstract: arXiv:2611.14013v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: The arteriolar-to-venular diameter ratio (AVR) is a clinically motivated marker of retinal vascular health. We present a five-stage pipeline for AVR estimation and exploratory retinopathy screening from fundus images, with inspectable intermediate outputs at each stage. The pipeline combines vessel and artery-vein masks, optic-disc localization, vessel-calibre estimation using a minimal-chord boundary walk, and AVR computation from dominant arterial and venular branches. An explicit threshold-based rule produces the screening decision, enabling errors to be traced to individual processing stages. On an exploratory cohort of 30 HRF images, we report 96.7% accuracy, an F1-score of 0.968 and ROC-AUC of 0.978. Ablation studies and an exploratory comparison with VascX examine the effects of vessel pairing, calibre measurement and aggregation. translated_title: 一种用于小动脉-静脉比值估计与视网膜病变筛查的分阶段可解释流水线
translated_abstract: 小动脉与静脉直径比值（AVR）是临床上评估视网膜血管健康的重要指标。我们提出了一种五阶段流水线，用于从眼底图像进行AVR估计和探索性视网膜病变筛查，每个阶段均提供可检查的中间输出。该流水线结合了血管与动静脉掩膜、视盘定位、基于最小弦边界游走法的血管管径估计，以及基于主要动脉和静脉分支的AVR计算。筛查决策由显式的阈值规则产生，使错误能够追溯到各个处理阶段。在包含30张HRF图像的探索性队列上，我们取得了96.7%的准确率、0.968的F1分数和0.978的ROC-AUC。消融实验以及与VascX的探索性对比研究考察了血管配对、管径测量和聚合方式的影响。受限于小规模队列、代理疾病标签以及缺乏独立参考标准，结果解读存在一定局限性。
tldr: 该论文提出了一种五阶段可解释流水线，通过可检查的中间输出和显式阈值规则实现眼底图像的AVR估计与视网膜病变筛查，使错误可追溯到具体处理阶段，并在30张HRF图像上达到96.7%的准确率。
